text: For seven months, Som Distilleries lost half its business. Not to a rival. To one licence.
In February, Madhya Pradesh suspended the licence of its Bhopal brewery. In June, the renewal was rejected. Ratings across the group were cut three times, the last one below investment grade.

The cost shows in the numbers. In the June quarter, total income fell to about two hundred and sixty nine crore rupees, from about five hundred and thirty crore a year earlier. Management said: we lost about two hundred and fifty crores of revenue.
Why not bring beer in from other states? Management said the import fees would make it a loss. In this business, the state licence is the moat.
On the twenty fourth of September, the High Court ordered the state to renew the licences within fifteen days. That is in the company's own filing.
But an order is not a running plant. The filings do not say when Bhopal restarts, or whether the state will appeal. And the rating is still below investment grade.
Educational research, not investment advice. Moat and Margin is not SEBI registered. Every fact here is from the company's own filings.
